newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fall on U.S. rate fears, seen down.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fall on U.S. rate fears, seen down.

text.p: Fears of a U.S. interest rate hike forced Russian share prices down on Thursday, traders said, and comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan after the market closed made further easing likely.

Some traders said the Russian market would slide on Friday morning unless the U.S. Dow Jones Industrial average, which fell over 50 points within minutes of Greenspan beginning a speech to Congress, recovered during the day.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index dropped 2.15 percent to 313.35 from 320.23 on a relatively low $30 million total market volume.
Power utility UES fell to $0.2040 from $0.2122 and LUKoil oil company dropped to $13.99 from $14.10.
"If the U.S. crashes, we have a problem here," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell chief equity trader Pavel Gronbjerg.
He said the market would wait for clear signals from the U.S. market and the end Russian-U.S. presidential summit in Helsinki on Friday.
Greenspan said that U.S. inflation was under control but the U.S. ideally should act pre-emptively to keep it low.
Traders said they had seen support for some shares at current levels and that second tiers had only slightly weakened.
But a senior Western trader said the market could ignore support.
"It is an emotional animal and could go right down through technical support levels."

Martin Diggle, director at Brunswick, said the Russian market's correlation with Western markets -- a new feature traders attribute to the presence of major new Western investors who entered the market in recent months -- could spur a five to 10 percent fall over the next week among leading shares.
"It looks like it will be even uglier tommorrow after Greenspan's comments," Diggle said.
